description: Under Computer Knowledge, Security Measures refer to the techniques and tools used to protect data, networks, and systems from unauthorized access and cyber attacks. This includes Firewalls, Antivirus software, and Encryption mechanisms.

sections.title: Cyber Security and Threats
sections.description: Primary threats that harm computer systems and networks, and the overarching concept of security.

key_concepts.explanation: The practice of protecting computers, servers, mobile devices, electronic systems, and networks from malicious digital attacks.
Malicious software specifically designed to disrupt, damage, or gain unauthorized access to a computer system (e.g., viruses, trojans, ransomware).
A social engineering technique used to fraudulently steal sensitive data, such as login credentials or credit card numbers, often via deceptive emails.

sections.title: Firewalls
sections.description: The first line of defense in network security that monitors and controls traffic.

key_concepts.explanation: A network security device or software that monitors incoming and outgoing network traffic and decides whether to allow or block specific traffic based on a defined set of security rules.
A firewall technique that analyzes data packets passing through a network and allows or blocks them based on predefined rules like IP addresses and ports.

key_associations.extra_info: A physical device positioned between a computer network and the internet, protecting the entire network from external threats.
A program installed on individual devices that regulates traffic specifically for that device (e.g., Windows Defender Firewall).

important_facts.fact: The term 'firewall' was originally coined for physical, fireproof walls built to prevent the spread of a fire within a building.

sections.title: Antivirus Software
sections.description: Programs designed to detect, prevent, and remove malicious software from a computer.

key_concepts.explanation: A utility software designed to search for, detect, prevent, and remove software viruses and other malicious software.
The process where antivirus software isolates infected files from the rest of the system in a safe location so they cannot spread or cause harm.
A unique, identifying pattern or string of code specific to a particular virus, used by antivirus software to recognize and neutralize threats.

historical_events.significance: A program named 'Reaper' was created to detect and remove the first computer virus called 'Creeper' on the ARPANET.

key_associations.extra_info: A built-in anti-malware component of Microsoft Windows operating systems.
Highly popular third-party security software suites used globally.

sections.title: Encryption and Cryptography
sections.description: The science of coding and decoding data to keep it secure and private.

key_concepts.explanation: The process of converting readable data (Plaintext) into an unreadable, scrambled format (Ciphertext) to prevent unauthorized access.
The reverse process of encryption, where ciphertext is converted back into its original, readable plaintext using a cryptographic key.

scientific_principles.formula_or_statement: A cryptographic method that uses the exact same secret key to both encrypt and decrypt data (e.g., AES).
scientific_principles.application: Ideal for quickly encrypting large databases and local files.

scientific_principles.formula_or_statement: A cryptographic method that uses a pair of keys: a Public Key for encryption and a Private Key for decryption (e.g., RSA).
scientific_principles.application: Widely used in securing internet communications and digital signatures.

important_facts.fact: End-to-End Encryption (E2EE) ensures that only the communicating users can read the messages, preventing third parties (even the service provider) from accessing the data.

sections.title: Important Security Protocols
sections.description: Standardized rules that secure data communication over the internet.

key_associations.associated_with: Secure Sockets Layer / Transport Layer Security
key_associations.extra_info: Cryptographic protocols designed to provide communications security over a computer network, commonly securing the link between a web server and a browser.
The secure, encrypted version of HTTP, primarily used to protect the privacy and integrity of exchanged data.
Establishes a protected network connection when using public networks, encrypting your internet traffic and disguising your online identity.

important_facts.fact: Two-Factor Authentication (2FA) adds an extra layer of security by requiring a user to provide two different authentication factors (like a password and an OTP) to verify themselves.
